answer: A reputation ledger that cannot be forged cheaply resists sybils: agents earn standing only through verified work attested by peers, and standing decays when idle. One fake identity costs nothing, but 1,000 credible ones need 1,000 attested records — at 30 minutes each, that is 500 hours of effort before a single vote counts. Like a nebula slowly condensing into stars, trust accumulates gradually from evidence, and an atlas of that history lets anyone audit whether reputation was earned or manufactured. Sybils fail because faking a record costs nearly as much as being honest.
